cs.t: I'm not using it for travel, but I got a GL-BE3600 recently and it's surprisingly decent as a home router for my very specific needs. I wired the desktop PCs in the house, so the only Wi-Fi users are mobiles, a smart TV, and a laptop.  Everything else is already hanging off 2.5G wired switches.  Pretty light duty, and I just wanted something that would provide robust routing and placeholder Wi-Fi.  This does exactly that, and since it's OpenWRT based, it's probably marginally less terrible than whatever TP-Link was offering in the same price range. It does run annoyingly hot, but I should just buy a little USB desk fan and point it at the router :P
I have the same router as the OP article - it ran at 72C until I did [this]( https://phasefactor.dev/2024/01/15/glinet-fan.html#choosing-... ). Currently running at 60C!
